abstract: We present an MBSE framework, implemented in SysML, that models the emergency medical response system for a network of rural clinics coordinating during a regional flood disaster.
journal: Journal of Rural Health Systems Engineering
title: A model-based systems engineering framework for rural emergency medical response

abstract: This study applies gradient-boosted machine learning models to sensor data from manufacturing equipment to predict mechanical failures before they occur, reducing unplanned downtime in urban factories.
title: Machine learning for predictive maintenance in industrial manufacturing plants

abstract: A retrospective analysis of emergency department overcrowding metrics at metropolitan hospitals during three influenza seasons, examining triage delays and resource allocation in a large urban health system.
title: Urban emergency department overcrowding during seasonal influenza outbreaks

abstract: Semi-structured interviews with 24 disaster relief coordinators in three coastal megacities explore organisational barriers to inter-agency coordination during flood response, without any computational modelling component.
title: Qualitative interviews with disaster relief coordinators in coastal megacities

abstract: An economic evaluation compares telemedicine-based triage against in-person triage for non-emergency complaints in remote mining communities, focusing on cost per consultation rather than disaster response.
title: Cost-effectiveness of telemedicine triage in remote mining communities
